# Quantitative reasoning that keeps the claim connected to the evidence

QMSBR is a modular learning library for social and behavioral research. It is
written for readers who have to make sense of quantitative studies: students
meeting these methods for the first time, researchers returning to them, and
anyone who has to judge whether a reported answer is warranted. Its first aim
is to show how a quantitative study answers its question, so that research
design, statistical reasoning, interpretation, and reproducible computing stay
connected and a software result never stands in for an argument.

The material is organized in parts. A part opens with a short **introduction**,
keeps its central concepts, symbols, and notation in a **concept reference**
you can consult while reading, and then works through its **chapters** in
reading order. **Part One** covers foundations, regression, and generalized
linear models; **Part Two** covers factor analysis and structural equation
modeling. The **R support** pages run R inside the browser, so there is nothing
to install before trying something out.

If you are new here, begin with the Part One introduction and then Chapter 1,
which sets up the reading that every later chapter uses. If you already know
where you are going, the collections below link to every page and its PDF.

## How to use this site

**Read online, or take the PDF.** Every chapter is a web page, which is the
better format for reading: responsive layout, a table of contents, search,
descriptive link text, and selectable code. The same chapter sits beside it as
a PDF for printing and annotation. Both carry the same content, and the PDF
link is on the chapter's line in the collections above.

**Look a concept up in the concept reference.** Each part gathers its central
concepts, symbols, and notation into one page of tables. Read a chapter for the
lesson; open the concept reference when you meet a symbol or a term and want
its definition and the chapter that develops it.

**Run the code in the browser.** The R support pages carry a live R session, so
you can run a chapter's analysis, change it, and see what changes without
installing anything. Your R workspace explains how to open, save, and reload
your own work, and the data sources page says where every dataset on the site
comes from and on what terms.

**A course may add its own materials.** QMSBR is a source library, not a
syllabus. Chapter identities and public links stay stable, so a course can
choose its own sequence and keep its schedule, announcements, assessment, and
answer keys in its own space while linking here for the readings.

## What comes next

::: {.roadmap-grid}
::: {.roadmap-card}
### Part One, Chapters 10–14

10. Interaction and Moderation
11. Binary Logistic Regression
12. Extending the GLM: Nominal, Ordinal, and Count Outcomes
13. Prediction, Cross-Validation, and Regularization
14. Regression Pitfalls and Causal Design
:::

::: {.roadmap-card}
### Part Two and Part Three

Part Two continues from confirmatory factor analysis into structural equation
modeling: models that relate latent variables to one another rather than only
to their indicators.

Part Three is reserved for multilevel and longitudinal models.
:::

::: {.roadmap-card}
### Supplementary chapters

A. How to Read a Quantitative Study as an Argument, and B. Extending the
Argument-Based Approach to Quantitative Studies, extend the argument-based
approach to coordinated questions, deeper evaluation, and regression-based
methods.
:::
:::

Later collections can join this same site when their scope is clear and their
material is ready.
